projects.title: Together We Rise
projects.description: A monumental sculpture created around the idea of Jamaica rising and rebuilding after Hurricane Melissa. The work incorporates a Tree of Life, representations of Jamaica’s 14 parishes through leaves, and scenes reflecting resilience, recovery and community.
projects.image_alt: Together We Rise monumental sculpture with clasped hands and a tree reaching into the sky
projects.page_intro: A 62-foot monument commissioned by Christopher Issa and S Hotels for St James Place on Jimmy Cliff Boulevard. Created in response to Hurricane Melissa, the work expresses Jamaica’s capacity to recover through collective effort.

page_blocks.label: Figures move from scenes of danger and rescue towards r
page_blocks.text: Figures move from scenes of danger and rescue towards rebuilding. A soldier reaches for a woman; workers and a farmer embody recovery. Above them, a Tree of Life carries healing plants representing Jamaica’s 14 parishes, linking renewal with the country’s landscape.

page_blocks.label: The sculpture honours local and international support a
page_blocks.text: The sculpture honours local and international support after the hurricane. Its interdependent figures turn resilience into a shared act, giving physical form to the idea that recovery depends on people helping one another.

page_blocks.label: The composition traces a passage from survival to hope.
page_blocks.text: The composition traces a passage from survival to hope. Its 62-foot height recalls Jamaica’s independence in 1962.

page_blocks.label: The process involved structural engineering, ground tes
page_blocks.text: The process involved structural engineering, ground testing and approvals, with particular attention to severe winds. Selected steel framing remains visible as part of the story of reconstruction.

page_blocks.label: Discarded materials from hurricane-affected communities
page_blocks.text: Discarded materials from hurricane-affected communities enter the work alongside sculpted forms. Planned planting and cascading water extend its connection to Jamaica’s natural environment.

projects.page_image_alt: Together We Rise monument under construction in Montego Bay, with intertwined hands and a Tree of Life

projects.title: Doctor Bird
projects.description: A monumental sculpture depicting Jamaica’s national bird, the Doctor Bird. The sculpture was constructed in eight sections due to its scale and took approximately three months to complete.
projects.image_alt: Doctor Bird monumental sculpture on the facade of S Hotel in Montego Bay
projects.page_intro: A 46-foot streamer-tail hummingbird created for the façade of S Hotel Montego Bay — transforming Jamaica's national bird into a landmark visible from Jimmy Cliff Boulevard.

page_blocks.label: Originally explored as a flatter wall treatment, the co
page_blocks.text: Originally explored as a flatter wall treatment, the concept developed into a dynamic three-dimensional bird that appears alive in space. Its scale required the sculpture to be fabricated outdoors in eight separate sections.

page_blocks.label: The finished work combines fibreglass, polystyrene foam
page_blocks.text: The finished work combines fibreglass, polystyrene foam and sheet metal, bringing sculptural expression and complex engineering together in a single architectural installation.

projects.title: Sintra Bronte
projects.description: A portrait inspired by Sintra Bronte’s iconic appearance in Jamaica’s 1972 tourism campaign, created using recycled materials.
projects.image_alt: Sintra Bronte portrait sculpture wearing the iconic Jamaica T-shirt

page_blocks.label: Commissioned by hotelier Christopher Issa, this portrai
page_blocks.text: Commissioned by hotelier Christopher Issa, this portrait by Scheed Cole and his team honours Sintra Bronte, the Trinidadian model featured in Jamaica’s iconic 1972 tourism campaign. Unveiled at Strings Restaurant at S Hotel Kingston in May 2024, the sculpture recreates her emergence from the water wearing the recognisable Jamaica T-shirt. The team used recycled materials, including plastic bags and cardboard.

projects.title: Natural History Museum of Jamaica
projects.description: A large-scale sculptural installation recreating Jamaican natural environments, including dry forests, wetlands, rainforest canopy, coral reefs, caves and marine environments. The project involved extensive research, mould-making, sculpting, painting and installation, incorporating recycled materials.
projects.image_alt: Mangrove wetland installation at the Natural History Museum of Jamaica
projects.page_intro: Sculptural environments created to make Jamaica's ecosystems feel tangible — from limestone caves and coral reefs to mangrove wetlands and forest canopy.

page_blocks.label: The permanent exhibition gallery contains six environme
page_blocks.text: The permanent exhibition gallery contains six environmental dioramas. Scheed researched specimens with botanists and zoologists, visited natural habitats, made drawing studies, sculpted forms by hand, moulded selected pieces, painted them and installed them in the museum.

page_blocks.text: The lifelike pieces were created using 360RM, a recycled composite developed by 360 Recycle Manufacturing.

projects.image_alt: Sculptural portraits at Montego Bay Legends Circle
projects.page_intro: Life-like sculptural portraiture bringing Jamaican heroes and cultural figures into public space.

page_blocks.label: At Montego Bay's Legends Circle, sculptural representat
page_blocks.text: At Montego Bay's Legends Circle, sculptural representations of National Heroes Samuel Sharpe and Marcus Garvey, National Heroine Nanny of the Maroons, and music legends Bob Marley and Jimmy Cliff create a public encounter with Jamaican identity.

page_blocks.label: The works combine Cole's commitment to realism with rec
page_blocks.text: The works combine Cole's commitment to realism with recycled-material innovation, making cultural memory visible, approachable and part of everyday public life.
